markdown:
## Why Career Pathing Matters

The #1 reason employees leave (after compensation) is lack of growth opportunity. LinkedIn's Workforce Learning Report shows that employees who see a clear career path stay 30% longer.

### Building Career Frameworks

#### Step 1: Define Levels

Create clear levels for every function:

Example: Engineering Career Ladder

| Level | Title | Scope | Typical Experience |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | Junior Engineer | Task execution | 0-2 years |
| L2 | Engineer | Feature ownership | 2-4 years |
| L3 | Senior Engineer | Project leadership | 4-7 years |
| L4 | Staff Engineer | Cross-team technical leadership | 7-12 years |
| L5 | Principal Engineer | Org-wide technical strategy | 12+ years |

#### Step 2: Define Competencies Per Level

For each level, specify expectations across dimensions:

- Technical skills
- Scope of impact
- Leadership and influence
- Communication
- Business acumen

#### Step 3: Create Assessment Criteria

Make promotion decisions transparent:

- Skills demonstration (projects, presentations, reviews)
- Peer feedback (360-degree input)
- Manager assessment
- Calibration across teams (ensure consistency)

#### Step 4: Enable Multiple Paths

Not everyone wants to be a manager. Create parallel tracks:

- Individual Contributor track (deep technical expertise)
- Management track (people leadership)
- Hybrid track (technical + some management)

### Career Conversations

Managers should conduct career development conversations quarterly:

- "Where do you see yourself in 2 years?"
- "What skills do you want to develop?"
- "What experiences would help you grow?"
- "How can I support your development?"
- "Are there projects or teams you are interested in?"

### Internal Mobility Programs

Companies with strong internal mobility:

- Fill 20-30% of roles internally
- Reduce external hiring costs
- Improve retention by 25%
- Build deeper institutional knowledge

Enable internal mobility through:

- Internal job board (all roles posted internally first)
- Cross-functional project assignments
- Rotation programs
- Internal mentoring across teams

### Measuring Career Pathing Impact

Track:

- Internal promotion rate (target: >15% annually)
- Time in role before promotion (healthy: 18-36 months)
- Internal mobility rate (% of roles filled internally)
- Employee satisfaction with growth opportunities (pulse survey)
- Voluntary turnover by level

When external hiring is needed, subscription sourcing fills gaps quickly while internal development continues.
